## Files

In Proteome Discoverer (2.4 to 3.x), open the consensus result and export the **Proteins**
page and the **Peptide Groups** page as text (File → Export → To Text (tab delimited), with
the per-file abundance columns included).

| Table | Export | Columns DiffPTM reads |
|---|---|---|
| total proteome | Proteins | `Accession`, `Gene Symbol`, `Contaminant`, `Abundances (Normalized): F1: Sample, <group>` (preferred) or `Abundance: F1: Sample, <group>` |
| PTM | Peptide Groups of the PTM-enriched analysis | `Master Protein Accessions`, `Sequence` (or `Annotated Sequence`), `Modifications in Master Proteins`, `Positions in Master Proteins`, `Contaminant`, the same abundance columns |

Each per-file abundance column names the file (`F1`, `F2`, ...), the quantification channel
(`Sample` for label-free, `126`, `127N`, ... for TMT) and the sample group; the sample name
kept by DiffPTM is `F1` (label-free) or `F1: 126` (TMT). The grouped, scaled and ratio
columns are not per-sample and are ignored.

Sites are read from **Modifications in Master Proteins**: `P12345 1xPhospho [S123(98.7)]`
gives residue S, position 123, localization probability 0.987 and modification Phospho;
`2xPhospho [S123(100); T127(95)]` gives a doubly modified peptidoform with multiplicity 2.
Carbamidomethyl, oxidation, acetyl and TMT labels are ignored.

The example files `inst/extdata/formats/ProteomeDiscoverer/` reproduce this layout.

## In the interface

1. **Import**: software *Proteome Discoverer*; upload `Proteins.txt` and
   `PeptideGroups.txt`.
2. **Design**: the samples are called `F1 ... F6` in both tables, so no renaming is needed
   when the two analyses were processed in the same study with the same files. When the
   enriched and proteome runs are different files (`F1`–`F6` proteome, `F7`–`F12` phospho),
   upload an annotation table that gives each file its condition (and a `subject` column
   shared by the paired files), or rename with two patterns. Conditions cannot be guessed
   from `F1`, so fill them from the annotation table or by editing the cells.
3. **Processing**: defaults. Peptide groups of the same site (missed cleavages, several
   charge states are already merged by PD) can be collapsed to sites with *Collapse
   peptidoforms to sites*.
4. **Statistics**, **Results**, **Download** as in the overview vignette.

## The same analysis in R

```{r import}
library(DiffPTM)
prot <- import_protein(fx("ProteomeDiscoverer", "Proteins.txt"), "Proteome Discoverer")
ptm  <- import_ptm(fx("ProteomeDiscoverer", "PeptideGroups.txt"), "Proteome Discoverer")
colnames(prot$intensity)
head(ptm$meta[, c("feature_id", "label", "stripped_sequence", "residue", "position", "localization_prob", "ptm_type", "multiplicity")])
```

The files are `F1 ... F6`; the annotation table maps them to conditions:

```{r analysis}
ann <- make_annotation(paste0("F", 1:6), rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 3), subject = rep(1:3, 2))
x <- new_ptm_experiment(prot, ptm, annotation = list(protein = ann, ptm = ann)) |>
  filter_flagged() |> filter_localization(0.75) |> filter_min_observed(min_n = 2) |>
  normalise(method = "global_median") |> match_ptm_to_protein("id")
x
res <- run_methods(x, make_contrasts(x, "vs_reference", reference = "control"), "limma", pi0_method = "bh")
res$label <- x$ptm$meta$label[match(res$feature_id, x$ptm$meta$feature_id)]
table(res$analysis, significant = res$adj_pvalue < 0.05)
```

```{r volcano, fig.height = 5}
plot_volcano(subset(res, analysis == "ptm_DPU"), fdr = 0.05, title = "PTM usage, treated vs control")
```

## TMT

With TMT, the abundance columns read `Abundance: F1: 126, control`, `Abundance: F1: 127N,
treated`, ...; the sample names become `F1: 126`, `F1: 127N`, ... Give the mixture (`F1`,
`F2`) in the `mixture` column of the design so that it enters the models as a batch effect,
and the subject when the same biological sample was labelled in both fractions.
